docs.title: bhavpy
docs.text:
Indian stock market data (NSE + BSE) from the exchanges' own public archives, as clean pandas DataFrames — with corporate-action adjusted prices you can audit, a local cache that makes repeat requests instant and offline, and a parser suite tested against the real servers every day.

pip install bhavpy

import bhavpy as bp

df = bp.history("RELIANCE", "2015-01-01")       # raw + adjusted OHLCV (IST dates)
bp.factors("RELIANCE", "2015-01-01")             # what was adjusted, by how much, and why
bp.constituents("NIFTY 50", as_of="2019-06-01")  # point-in-time index members
  • Quickstart — the main calls in five minutes.
  • Adjusted prices — how the headline feature works and how to check it.
  • Cookbook — NIFTY 50 history, adjusted returns, a moving-average backtest, an implied-volatility smile.
  • Reliability — what is solid, what is fragile, and why.
  • Research & sources — every URL used, coverage, terms of use, and how bhavpy compares with other libraries.

Disclaimer

Not affiliated with NSE or BSE. Data is for personal/research use and you are responsible for following the exchanges' terms of use. Not investment advice. See the full disclaimer.

docs.title: Adjusted prices
docs.text: Getting Indian corporate actions right is the main reason bhavpy exists.

docs.title: What gets adjusted
docs.text:
Each corporate action becomes a price factor multiplied into every price before its ex-date. Factors of later events multiply, so the newest prices are never changed and older prices are expressed in today's share terms (relative to the last row returned).

Action (NSE wording) Factor Example Face value split, From Rs 10 To Rs 2 new FV / old FV 0.2 Consolidation, From Rs 1 To Rs 10 new FV / old FV 10 Bonus a:b (a new for every b held) b / (a + b) 1:1 → 0.5, 1:2 → 0.667 Rights a:b @ Premium Rs P TERP / Pcum, TERP = (b·Pcum + a·S)/(a+b), S = P + face value RELIANCE 2020: 0.9906 Dividend Rs D (only adjust="total") (Pcum − D) / Pcum CRSP-style total return Demerger / scheme of arrangement estimated: ex-day price-discovery open / Pcum (close if the open was stale); check="estimated". demerger="ignore" leaves it unadjusted RELIANCE 2023 (Jio Financial): 0.908

Pcum is the last close before the ex-date. Volumes are scaled by the inverse factor for splits, consolidations and bonuses.

docs.title: Where the ratios come from
docs.text:
NSE's corporate-actions feed (the same data as the Corporate Actions page on nseindia.com), cached locally. The free-text subjects ("Fv Splt Frm Rs 10 To Rs 2", "Int Div-Rs.2.50/- Per Share Purpose Revised", ...) are parsed by bhavpy.sources.nse_corpactions.parse_subject, tested on the spellings found in ~9,000 real records from 2010–2026.

Note: the bhavcopy's own prev_close is not rebased on ex-dates, so it cannot be used to infer adjustments (see research).

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
• Price check. For splits, bonuses and consolidations bhavpy compares the expected factor (all such events on one ex-date multiplied together) with the actual overnight move open(ex-date) / close(day before). If they differ by more than 25%, the record is marked check="mismatch", not applied, and a warning is raised. Pass on_mismatch="apply" to apply it anyway.
  • Gap scan. Overnight moves beyond −23%/+30% that match a common split/bonus ratio within 6% but have no record are reported as kind="unexplained_gap". They are applied only with infer=True — or automatically if the corporate-actions feed could not be reached, so adjustment still works when NSE's site is down.

docs.title: Inspect everything
docs.text:
f = bp.factors("RELIANCE", "2005-01-01", adjust="total")
f[["ex_date", "kind", "ratio", "amount", "price_factor", "cumulative_factor", "check", "source"]]

The same table is attached to every adjusted frame as df.attrs["events"].

docs.title: Validated examples (in the unit tests)
docs.text:
Stock Ex-date Action Raw move Adjusted move RELIANCE 2017-09-07 bonus 1:1 (legacy file format) −50.3% −0.6% RELIANCE 2024-10-28 bonus 1:1 (UDiFF format) −49.8% +0.5% SHRIRAMFIN 2025-01-10 split FV 10 → 2 −81.1% −5.3% RELIANCE 2020-05-13 rights 1:15 @ ₹1,257 factor 0.9906 (TERP) RELIANCE 2026-06-05 dividend ₹6 (total) factor (P−6)/P BAJFINANCE 2025-06-16 bonus 4:1 and split FV 2 → 1 on one day ≈ −90% continuous (combined factor 0.1) RELIANCE 2023-07-20 Jio Financial demerger −9.2% factor 2,580 / 2,841.85 (price discovery)

Whole-index checks (python scripts/validate_adjustment.py "NIFTY 500", run on the full 2015–2026 cache on 2026-10-21): across the 499 NIFTY 500 members with data, 340 corporate actions were applied to 211 stocks with zero price-check mismatches; one overnight jump was flagged as an unexplained gap (FORCEMOT 2024-02-14, a genuine +33% results-day move — reported, not applied). The largest adjusted daily moves are all real market events (YESBANK 2020-03-06, RPOWER 2019-02-04, POLICYBZR 2026-09-24, ...).

For the NIFTY 50 alone: for all 50 NIFTY 50 members, the largest adjusted daily move is the March 2020 COVID crash or a known event-day move (e.g. AXISBANK −28% on 2020-03-23) — no split, bonus or rights date shows up as a jump. The only ex-dates that needed the demerger estimate were ADANIENT 2015-06-03, TMPV (Tata Motors) 2025-10-14, RELIANCE 2023-07-20, ITC 2025-01-06 and HINDUNILVR 2025-12-05.

The live suite repeats the RELIANCE 2024 check against the real servers every day.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text:
Daily OHLCV history for NSE stocks and indices, raw and corporate-action adjusted.

Corporate-action adjustment: the factors, where they came from, and whether prices agree.

How it works
  1. Corporate actions come from NSE's own corporate-actions feed (cached), parsed by :func:bhavpy.sources.nse_corpactions.parse_subject.
  2. Each event becomes a price factor applied to every price before its ex-date:

============== ========================================= =========================== action factor example ============== ========================================= =========================== split new FV / old FV FV 10 -> 2 : 0.2 consolidation new FV / old FV FV 1 -> 10 : 10 bonus a:b b / (a + b) 1:1 : 0.5 rights a:b @S TERP / P, TERP = (bP + aS) / (a + b) only when S < P dividend D (P - D) / P (adjust="total" only) CRSP-style total return ============== ========================================= ===========================

P is the last close before the ex-date (the cum price). 3. Price check. For splits, bonuses and consolidations the overnight move open(ex) / P must be within 25% of the factor. If the market says otherwise the record is reported with check="mismatch" and not applied (configurable). 4. Gap scan. Overnight jumps that look like a split/bonus but have no matching record are reported as unexplained_gap (and applied only with infer=True, or automatically when the corporate-action feed is unreachable).

The output of :func:factors shows every event, its factor, its source and its check, so the adjustment is fully auditable.

Index constituents: current (NSE Indices files) and point-in-time.

Point-in-time membership avoids survivorship bias in backtests:

  • NIFTY 50 - reconstructed by walking NSE's published index changes (bundled in data/nifty50_changes.csv, each row citing the NSE press release) back from today's list. Covers 2016-04-01 onwards; the walk is verified to keep exactly 50 names.
  • Other indices - bhavpy stores a dated snapshot each time it downloads a list, so history builds up from your first use (or from a scheduled bhavpy update).

Symbol master: current listings, ISINs, symbol/name changes, delistings.

Old tickers keep working: bhavpy.history("ZOMATO") resolves to ETERNAL and stitches both symbols' history together, using NSE's own symbol-change file.

Futures & options: daily bhavcopy, futures history, live option chain, lots, expiries.

NSE trading calendar: holidays, special sessions (Muhurat, Budget-day, DR drills), expiries.

Sources, in order of trust:

  1. NSE holiday-master API (2011 onwards, incl. future scheduled holidays), cached.
  2. A bundled calendar (data/nse_calendar.csv) built from the API plus the bhavcopy archive itself: a weekday with no bhavcopy is a closure, a weekend/holiday with one is a special session. This covers 2005 onwards and works offline.
  3. Days the cache has seen (a settled 404 for a weekday = closure).

Institutional flows and large trades: FII/DII cash activity, bulk and block deals.

BSE daily equity data and NSE <-> BSE mapping by ISIN.

bhavpy update: bring the cache up to date incrementally.

Runtime settings: cache location, politeness limits, timeouts.

Change them with :func:bhavpy.configure or environment variables (BHAVPY_CACHE_DIR, BHAVPY_RATE, BHAVPY_OFFLINE).

Exception hierarchy.

Every error raised by bhavpy derives from :class:BhavpyError, so callers can catch one type. The subclasses say why something failed, because the fix is different in each case: wait and retry, update the library, or check the input.

docs.title: history(symbol, start=None, end=None, *, adjust='split', series=None, infer=None, on_mismatch='skip', demerger='estimate')
docs.text:
Daily OHLCV for an NSE stock (or index) from the official bhavcopy archive.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default symbol str

NSE ticker ("RELIANCE"), an old ticker ("ZOMATO"), or an index name ("NIFTY 50", "BANKNIFTY", "INDIA VIX").

required start DateLike

Any date-like; default is the last 365 days.

None end DateLike

Any date-like; default is the last 365 days.

None adjust str | None

"split" (default) adjusts for splits, bonuses, consolidations and rights; "total" also for dividends (use for return calculations); None = raw only. Adjusted prices are expressed in the share terms of the last row returned.

'split' demerger str

"estimate" (default) adjusts demergers/schemes using the ex-date price discovery (flagged check="estimated"); "ignore" leaves them unadjusted.

'estimate' series Sequence[str] | None

Restrict to series, e.g. ["EQ"]. Default picks the best series per day (EQ, then BE, BZ, ...), so stocks moved to trade-to-trade stay continuous.

None

Returns:

Type Description DataFrame indexed by IST date with raw ``open high low close last prev_close volume turnover trades`` and, when adjusted, ``adj_open adj_high adj_low adj_close adj_volume adj_factor``. ``df.attrs["events"]`` holds the factor table.

docs.title: build_events(actions, prices, *, mode='split', infer=None, on_mismatch='skip', demerger='estimate')
docs.text:
Turn corporate-action records + raw prices into an auditable factor table.

prices is a raw daily frame indexed by IST date with open and close. mode: "split" (splits, bonuses, rights) or "total" (also dividends). infer: apply split-like price gaps with no record (None = only if feed failed). on_mismatch: "skip" or "apply" records the price check contradicts. demerger: "estimate" (default; see :func:_demerger_factor) or "ignore".

Full F&O bhavcopy for one day (default: latest available): futures and options.

The raw file is cached once (~1 MB/day); futures rows also go into the futures table.

Daily futures OHLC/OI for symbol.

docs.title: expiry_calendar(symbol='NIFTY', start=None, end=None)
docs.text:
Historical + scheduled expiry dates for symbol's derivatives.

Built from F&O bhavcopies sampled once a week (every listed expiry appears in each day's file), so a decade costs ~500 downloads once, then it is cached.

docs.title: option_chain(symbol='NIFTY', expiry=None)
docs.text:
Live option-chain snapshot (long format: one row per strike x CE/PE).

This is the one dataset that only exists on NSE's live site; it is fetched with a normal browser-like request and never cached for more than a minute. df.attrs holds timestamp and underlying_price.

docs.title: history(code, start=None, end=None)
docs.text:
Daily OHLCV for a BSE security by scrip code ("500325"), ISIN, or BSE ticker.

BSE tickers exist in the files only from 2024-07-08; scrip code and ISIN work for the whole archive. Prices are unadjusted (corporate actions: use the NSE series).

docs.title: nse_bse_map(day=None)
docs.text:
Securities listed on both exchanges, joined by ISIN.

Columns: isin, nse_symbol, nse_series, bse_code, bse_symbol, bse_group, name.

docs.title: update(start=None, *, indices_only=False)
docs.text:
Fetch every missing day since the last cached day (or since start).

Updates: NSE equity bhavcopies, NSE index closes, FII/DII flows, symbol lists and constituent snapshots. Returns a summary dict. Safe to run repeatedly (e.g. daily from cron or a scheduled GitHub Action): settled days are never re-downloaded.

docs.text:
Change settings, e.g. bhavpy.configure(cache_dir="~/data/bhavpy", rate=2).

Returns the active :class:Settings.

docs.title: BhavpyError
docs.text:
Bases: Exception

Base class for all bhavpy errors.

docs.title: NotAvailable
docs.text:
Bases: BhavpyError

The exchange has no file for this request (holiday, not yet published, or before the archive starts). Not a bug: the data simply does not exist at the source.

docs.title: BlockedError
docs.text:
Bases: BhavpyError

The exchange refused the request (HTTP 401/403/429, or a bot-check page).

bhavpy never tries to get around such blocks. Wait a while, lower the request rate (bhavpy.configure(rate=...)), or use the archive-based functions, which are rarely blocked.

docs.title: FormatChanged
docs.text:
Bases: BhavpyError

A file or JSON response no longer has the shape bhavpy expects.

This usually means the exchange changed a URL or column layout. Please open an issue with the message text; the daily live test suite normally catches these within a day.

docs.title: SymbolNotFound
docs.text:
Bases: BhavpyError

The symbol could not be resolved, even through rename/delisting history.

docs.title: NetworkError
docs.text:
Bases: BhavpyError

The request failed after all retries (timeouts, DNS, connection resets).

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
bhavpy download SYMBOL [--from DATE] [--to DATE] [--adjusted [split|total]] [--only-adjusted] [-o FILE]
bhavpy factors SYMBOL [--from DATE] [--total] [-o FILE]
bhavpy update [--from DATE] [--indices-only]
bhavpy constituents [INDEX] [--as-of DATE] [-o FILE]
bhavpy chain [SYMBOL] [--expiry DATE] [-o FILE]
bhavpy market [--date DATE] [--exchange nse|bse] [-o FILE]
bhavpy holidays [YEAR]
bhavpy symbol SYMBOL
bhavpy flows [--history] [-o FILE]
bhavpy deals bulk|block [--from DATE] [--to DATE] [-o FILE]
bhavpy cache info|path|vacuum|clear [--dataset NAME]

Global options: --cache-dir, --rate, --offline, -q/--quiet, -v/--verbose.

Output format follows the file extension: .csv (default), .parquet (needs pip install "bhavpy[parquet]"), .json, .jsonl, .xlsx (needs openpyxl). Without -o, CSV goes to stdout, so you can pipe: bhavpy download TCS | head.

Examples:

bhavpy download RELIANCE --from 2015-01-01 --adjusted -o reliance.csv
bhavpy download "NIFTY 50" --from 2013-01-01 -o nifty.parquet
bhavpy constituents "NIFTY 50" --as-of 2018-06-01
bhavpy symbol ZOMATO           # -> ETERNAL, ISIN, rename history

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install bhavpy            # pandas + requests only
pip install "bhavpy[plot]"    # + matplotlib/scipy for the cookbook plots

Python 3.10–3.13 on Linux, macOS and Windows.

docs.title: Stock history
docs.text:
import bhavpy as bp

df = bp.history("TCS", "2020-01-01", "2024-12-31")
df.columns
# symbol series isin open high low close last prev_close volume turnover trades
# adj_open adj_high adj_low adj_close adj_last adj_prev_close adj_volume adj_factor
  • The index is the trading date, timezone-aware in Asia/Kolkata.
  • adjust="split" (default) handles splits, consolidations, bonuses and rights; adjust="total" also handles dividends (use it for returns); adjust=None gives raw prices.
  • Old tickers work: bp.history("ZOMATO", ...) returns ZOMATO rows before 9 Apr 2025 and ETERNAL rows after, in one frame.
  • The first long request downloads the whole market for those days (one file per day) into the cache. Later requests for any stock in that range are instant and work offline.

bp.constituents("NIFTY 50", as_of="2018-06-01")

bp.option_chain("NIFTY")                    # live snapshot (bid/ask, OI, IV)

docs.title: Calendar, flows, deals, BSE

bp.fii_dii(); bp.bulk_deals("2026-10-01"); bp.block_deals("2026-09-01")

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
bp.configure(cache_dir="~/data/bhavpy", rate=2, offline=False, progress=True)

or environment variables BHAVPY_CACHE_DIR, BHAVPY_RATE, BHAVPY_OFFLINE=1.

docs.title: Keeping data fresh
docs.text:
bhavpy update --from 2015-01-01   # first time: backfill
bhavpy update                     # afterwards: only missing days (cron / Task Scheduler)

update also stores today's FII/DII numbers and index-constituent snapshots, so running it daily builds history that NSE itself does not keep online.

docs.title: Async
docs.text:
import asyncio, bhavpy.aio as bpa
frames = asyncio.run(asyncio.gather(*(bpa.history(s, "2024-01-01") for s in ["TCS", "INFY"])))

The global rate limit still applies across concurrent calls.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Exception Meaning NotAvailable the exchange has no file for that request (holiday, not yet published, before archive start) BlockedError the exchange refused (HTTP 401/403/429 or a bot page). bhavpy never bypasses this; wait, or lower rate FormatChanged a file layout changed — please open an issue with the message SymbolNotFound no rows for that symbol/range, even through renames

All inherit from bp.BhavpyError.

docs.title: Reliability: what is solid, what is fragile
docs.text: Feature Source Rating Why Equity OHLCV history NSE bhavcopy archive (1994 →) Solid Static files; URLs unchanged for years except the July 2024 UDiFF switch, which bhavpy handles. Cached forever once downloaded. Index history NSE ind_close_all archive (2012-03 →) Solid Static daily files. Old index names are mapped. Gap: no pre-2012 index history in this archive. Symbol master, renames, delistings NSE CSV files Solid Plain CSVs; cached; stale copy used if a refresh fails. F&O bhavcopy, futures, lot sizes NSE archives Solid Static files. BSE bhavcopy BSE download files (2017 →) Good Static files, but BSE returns its HTML shell (HTTP 200) for missing days; bhavpy detects that. Pre-2017 files are no longer served. Current index constituents niftyindices.com CSVs Good Static per-index files; file codes could be renamed. Point-in-time NIFTY 50 bundled change log since 2016 Good Validated every day: reconstructed members must have traded. Must be extended when NSE changes the index (twice a year); a test fails if today's list stops matching. Point-in-time for other indices local snapshots Limited Only from your first bhavpy update; NSE publishes no free history. Adjustment ratios NSE corporate-actions JSON Good JSON endpoint (could change), but cached per symbol, every record is price-checked, and if the feed is unreachable bhavpy falls back to inferring splits/bonuses from price gaps. Demergers are not adjusted automatically. Holidays NSE holiday API (2011 →) + bundled calendar (2005 →) Solid Works offline from the bundled file. Option chain NSE live JSON (option-chain-v3) Fragile Live website endpoint; NSE has retired previous versions (option-chain-indices now 404) and may add bot protection. Only snapshot; no history. FII/DII NSE live JSON Fragile Latest day only; history exists only if you run update daily. Bulk/block deal history NSE live JSON Fragile Website endpoint; the daily CSV archive is used for today's deals as a fallback source.

docs.title: What happens when something breaks
docs.text:
• bhavpy raises FormatChanged with the URL and the columns it saw, instead of returning wrong data.
  • The live workflow runs every day and opens an issue labelled source-broken within 24 hours.
  • The fix is one module in src/bhavpy/sources/; see CONTRIBUTING.md.
  • Cached data keeps working (bp.configure(offline=True)).

docs.title: Politeness
docs.text:
• At most 3 requests/s per host by default (bp.configure(rate=...)), 3 parallel workers.
  • Retries with exponential backoff and jitter on 429/5xx/connection errors.
  • An honest bhavpy/<version> token in the User-Agent.
  • Each archive file is downloaded once; days with no file (holidays) are remembered.
  • bhavpy never solves CAPTCHAs, never retries around a 403 more than once, and never uses logins or paid APIs.

docs.title: Research notes (checked live on 2026-10-21)
docs.text: Everything below was checked against the live sites and package indexes on 2026-10-21, not from memory. Re-run pytest -m live tests/live to re-verify the data-source claims; the scheduled CI job does this every day.

GPL licence limits reuse. nsepy 0.8 (2020-03-07) 807 / 164 old www1.nseindia.com pages Dead: the old NSE site it scraped was retired. yfinance .NS / .BO 1.7.0 (2026-08-26) 25.6k / 108 Yahoo Finance Not exchange data. Reports of wrong/missing NSE data (#2055, #2022, #2612), splits not applied (#1531), dividend-date errors (#2377); users report wrong Indian dividends and demergers (Quantra thread, TradingQnA thread). No delisted names, no F&O, no constituents, no bhavcopy turnover/trades, adjustment not auditable. nsetools 2.0.1 (2025-03-18) 908 / 2 NSE live quotes Live quotes only, no history. bsedata 0.6.0 (2024-03-14) 116 / 4 BSE live quotes Live quotes only. openchart 0.2.0 (2026-01-16) 83 / 10 NSE charting API Intraday/EOD candles; no adjustment, no corporate actions, no cache. nsefin 0.1.5 (2025-09-08) – NSE live JSON Young, small surface.

Common pattern: most libraries wrap NSE's live website JSON, which changes often and is bot-protected, and none publishes a test that runs against the real site. That is why "X stopped working" is the most common issue type above.

BSE equity bhavcopy www.bseindia.com/download/BhavCopy/Equity/BhavCopy_BSE_CM_0_0_0_YYYYMMDD_F_0000.CSV, legacy EQ_ISINCODE_DDMMYY.zip UDiFF 2024-07-08 →; legacy 2017-01 → 2024-07-05 Missing files come back as HTTP 200 with the site's HTML shell. Pre-2017 legacy files are no longer served.

Live JSON endpoints on www.nseindia.com/api/... (worked on 2026-10-21 without cookies with a browser-like User-Agent and a Referer: https://www.nseindia.com/ header):

Endpoint Used for Status holiday-master?type=trading&year=YYYY trading calendar works, years 2011–2026 corporates-corporateActions?index=equities&symbol=X&from_date=&to_date= splits/bonus/rights/dividends works, history back to the 2000s option-chain-contract-info?symbol=X expiries, strikes works option-chain-v3?type=Indices\|Equity&symbol=X&expiry=DD-Mon-YYYY option chain snapshot works fiidiiTradeReact FII/DII cash flows (latest day only) works historicalOR/bulk-block-short-deals?optionType=bulk_deals\|block_deals&from=&to= deal history works option-chain-indices, equity-stockIndices (used by older libraries) 404, retired historical/cm/equity (used by jugaad-data / nsepython) bot-check HTML page for scripted clients; bhavpy does not use it

Headers: the archive host drops connections from a bare non-browser User-Agent; a browser User-Agent with an honest bhavpy/<version> suffix works. The www.nseindia.com home page answers 403 to scripted clients; bhavpy never needs it, and does not try to get around it. api.bseindia.com also answers 403; bhavpy uses only BSE's download files.

Other checked sources: the niftyindices.com historical-data POST endpoint returned an error, and the NSE "PR" zip (archives/equities/bhavcopy/pr/PRDDMMYY.zip) is not served for 2008. Neither is needed.

docs.title: An important finding for adjustment
docs.text: The bhavcopy PREVCLOSE / PrvsClsgPric field is not rebased on split/bonus ex-dates. On RELIANCE's 1:1 bonus (ex-date 2017-09-07) the file shows close 818.10 and prev close 1645.40; on the 2024-10-28 bonus it shows 1334.35 and 2655.70. So adjustment cannot be derived from the bhavcopy alone; bhavpy uses NSE's corporate-actions feed for the ratios and checks each one against the actual overnight price move. Dividends are also not reflected in prev close (RELIANCE ex-dividend 2026-06-05: prev close 1303.70 = previous day's close).

docs.title: 3. Terms of use
docs.text:
• NSE (nseindia.com terms, read 2026-10-21): "User is prohibited to conduct any systematic or automated data collection activities (including scraping, data mining, data extraction and data harvesting) on or in relation to our Website / Mobile Application." It also says content shall not be "copied, modified ... reproduced, ... distributed ... sold". NSE's robots.txt allows / and disallows only /market-data-test.
  • NSE Indices (niftyindices.com terms): "You may not conduct any systematic or automated data collection activities ... without our express written consent" and the site "may be used only ... for personal, non-commercial use only."
  • BSE: the terms pages are JavaScript-only and could not be read by an automated fetch. BSE's published disclaimers say material may not be reproduced or redistributed without prior written permission (example). Treat BSE data with the same restrictions as NSE's.

What this means for bhavpy and its users. The exchanges' terms restrict automated collection and redistribution. bhavpy is a tool that an individual runs on their own machine; it does not host or redistribute data. It keeps load low (archive files, local cache, 3 requests/s cap, incremental updates), identifies itself in the User-Agent, never bypasses blocks, cookies walls or CAPTCHAs, and stops with a clear error when refused. Users are responsible for complying with the exchanges' terms, including getting permission where required. For commercial use or redistribution, license data from NSE (NSE Data & Analytics) or BSE, or an authorised vendor.

docs.title: 5. Name
docs.text:
Candidates (all free on PyPI on 2026-10-21; none taken under rishitmpatel on GitHub):

  1. bhavpy — bhav means "price" in Hindi/Gujarati/Marathi and is the root of bhavcopy, the exchange file the library is built on. Short, pronounceable, says what it does to anyone in Indian markets, no exchange trademark in it.
  2. dalalpy — after Dalal Street. Catchy, but evokes BSE specifically and "dalal" also means "broker/middleman".
  3. tejimandi — "bull/bear market" in Hindi. Fun, but long, and a well-known Indian advisory app already uses the name Teji Mandi.

Pick: bhavpy. (PyPI names bhav and bhavcopy are taken by unrelated small projects; bhavpy is distinct.)

docs.title: Build adjusted returns
docs.text:
Use adjust="total" for return calculations: it adjusts for dividends as well as splits, bonuses and rights, so adj_close.pct_change() is a total-return series.

import bhavpy as bp
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

df = bp.history("RELIANCE", "2015-01-01", adjust="total")

raw = df["close"].pct_change()
adj = df["adj_close"].pct_change()
print(raw.min(), adj.min())       # raw has -50% "crashes" on bonus ex-dates; adjusted does not

cagr = (df["adj_close"].iloc[-1] / df["adj_close"].iloc[0]) ** (252 / len(df)) - 1
vol = np.log(df["adj_close"]).diff().std() * np.sqrt(252)
print(f"CAGR {cagr:.1%}, annualised vol {vol:.1%}")

docs.title: Returns for many stocks at once
docs.text:
syms = ["TCS", "INFY", "HDFCBANK", "ICICIBANK", "ETERNAL"]
rets = pd.DataFrame({s: bp.history(s, "2020-01-01", adjust="total")["adj_close"] for s in syms}).pct_change()
rets.corr().round(2)

The first call downloads the whole market for the range once; the other symbols come from the cache. ETERNAL automatically includes its history as ZOMATO.

docs.title: Split-only vs total
docs.text: adjust="split" adjust="total" Splits, consolidations, bonuses, rights ✓ ✓ Dividends – ✓ Use for charts, price levels, technical indicators returns, performance, factor research

docs.title: Option chain → implied-volatility smile
docs.text:
bp.option_chain() returns a live snapshot in long format (one row per strike and CE/PE), including NSE's own implied volatility. You can also compute IV yourself from the mid price with Black-Scholes.

import bhavpy as bp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

chain = bp.option_chain("NIFTY")                  # nearest expiry
spot = chain.attrs["underlying_price"]
print(chain.attrs["timestamp"], spot)

# Out-of-the-money options carry the smile: puts below spot, calls above.
otm = chain[((chain.option_type == "PE") & (chain.strike < spot)) |
            ((chain.option_type == "CE") & (chain.strike >= spot))]
otm = otm[otm.iv > 0]

for side, leg in otm.groupby("option_type"):       # puts left of spot, calls right
    plt.plot(leg.strike, leg.iv, "o-", label=side)
plt.axvline(spot, ls="--", c="grey"); plt.legend()
plt.xlabel("strike"); plt.ylabel("IV (%)"); plt.title("NIFTY IV smile (NSE IV)")

docs.title: Compute IV yourself
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq
from scipy.stats import norm
import pandas as pd

def bs_price(S, K, T, r, sigma, kind):
    d1 = (np.log(S / K) + (r + sigma**2 / 2) * T) / (sigma * np.sqrt(T))
    d2 = d1 - sigma * np.sqrt(T)
    if kind == "CE":
        return S * norm.cdf(d1) - K * np.exp(-r * T) * norm.cdf(d2)
    return K * np.exp(-r * T) * norm.cdf(-d2) - S * norm.cdf(-d1)

def implied_vol(price, S, K, T, r, kind):
    try:
        return brentq(lambda s: bs_price(S, K, T, r, s, kind) - price, 1e-4, 5.0)
    except ValueError:
        return np.nan

expiry = chain["expiry"].iloc[0]
now = pd.Timestamp.now(tz="Asia/Kolkata")
T = max((expiry + pd.Timedelta(hours=15, minutes=30) - now).total_seconds(), 3600) / (365 * 24 * 3600)
r = 0.065                                          # approx. risk-free rate

otm = otm.assign(mid=(otm.bid + otm.ask) / 2)
otm["my_iv"] = [implied_vol(m, spot, k, T, r, t) * 100 for m, k, t in zip(otm.mid, otm.strike, otm.option_type)]
otm[["strike", "option_type", "mid", "iv", "my_iv"]]

Info

The option chain is the one dataset bhavpy reads from NSE's live website (there is no archive for it). Outside market hours you get the last snapshot. For end-of-day history of options use bp.fno.options("NIFTY", "2026-10-19") from the F&O bhavcopy.

nifty[["open", "high", "low", "close", "pe", "pb", "div_yield"]].tail()

docs.title: All 50 members' prices, point-in-time
docs.text:
members = bp.constituents("NIFTY 50", as_of="2020-01-01")["symbol"]
closes = {s: bp.history(s, "2020-01-01", "2020-12-31")["adj_close"] for s in members}
panel = pd.DataFrame(closes)          # 2020 prices of the members *as of Jan 2020*

Using the as-of list (rather than today's members) avoids survivorship bias: YESBANK, for example, was a member in January 2020 and is included.

docs.title: Simple moving-average backtest
docs.text:
A long-only 50/200-day crossover on adjusted prices. It trades on the next day's close after a signal, to avoid look-ahead bias.

import bhavpy as bp
import numpy as np

px = bp.history("TCS", "2015-01-01", adjust="total")["adj_close"]

fast, slow = px.rolling(50).mean(), px.rolling(200).mean()
signal = (fast > slow).astype(int)
position = signal.shift(1).fillna(0)            # act the day after the signal

ret = px.pct_change().fillna(0)
cost = 0.001 * position.diff().abs().fillna(0)  # 10 bps per change in position
strat = position * ret - cost

def stats(r):
    curve = (1 + r).cumprod()
    years = len(r) / 252
    cagr = curve.iloc[-1] ** (1 / years) - 1
    sharpe = r.mean() / r.std() * np.sqrt(252)
    dd = (curve / curve.cummax() - 1).min()
    return f"CAGR {cagr:6.1%}  Sharpe {sharpe:4.2f}  MaxDD {dd:6.1%}"

print("buy & hold:", stats(ret))
print("SMA 50/200:", stats(strat))

Why adjusted prices matter here: on a raw series every bonus or split looks like a crash, which flips the moving averages and creates fake trades. With adjust="total" the series is continuous and dividends are counted in the return.

Note

This is a teaching example, not a trading system and not investment advice.
